observation.visible_scene: A red disc (frisbee-like) is wedged into a layer of snow capping a horizontal wooden rail. The background shows a blurred snowy yard and a light-colored house. The rail, its dark knots, and the background stay in fixed positions throughout the clip, indicating a static camera.
visible_changes: The red disc translates slowly to the right along the snow-covered rail; its left edge moves from the left third toward the center and its right edge approaches the right-side knot.
A shallow groove/indentation opens in the snow on the disc's left side, marking the space it has vacated.
The visible red portion of the disc shrinks vertically while the white snow cap on its top thickens, so the disc appears to sink deeper into / become more buried by the snow.
Faint tiny white specks appear intermittently in the air above the rail (possible light snowfall or blown snow, not certain).
outside_clip_unknowns: How the disc originally came to rest on the rail.
What drives the rightward sliding and the apparent sinking.
Whether the motion continues, stops, or the disc falls off after the last sampled frame.
uncertain_details: Whether the small airborne specks are real snow or compression noise.
Whether the reduced red height is true sinking or simply more snow covering the top.
Exact speed/acceleration of the slide, given only sparse time samples.
